messages.author: e2969220f16d5020
messages.subject: Creating graphs for the first time
parts:
Hello,

I am a beginner in R.

I am learning graphs right now but finding it bit confusing to do.

I have 2 variables, I want to put them on a scatter plot, make the y axis a log scale showing values as (10^n) not 1E+5, the x axis is normal, add a trendline to the points then have that line equation.


So far I done this:


x<-c(0, 10, 20)
y<-c(39600000, 2100000, 122000))
plot(x, y, log = "y", type = "b", pch = "21: circle", col = "black", ylab = "CFU/ml", xlab = "Time", frame.plot = FALSE)


So when I run the above, I get the picture #1, attached. Technically it is alright but the format is very bad.

Starting with the y axies, how can I change the scale to show 10^4 - 10^9 instead the weird number format that has the letter e in it. (similar to picture #2, attached).
I can't understand why my data point are showing as the number 2 instead of an empty circle with size 21, is my pch argument wrong? 
Finally, how can I obtain the linear equation for the line? I can't seem to find a command to do it?


I would really appreciate your help.


Thanks,
Yousef

messages.author: b88baf3c67a479f2
messages.subject: Re: Creating graphs for the first time
parts:
How about:
fancy_scientific <- function(l) {
  # citation:
  # https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11610377/how-do-i-change-the-formatting-of-numbers-on-an-axis-with-ggplot
  # turn in to character string in scientific notation
  l <- format(l, scientific = TRUE)
  # quote the part before the exponent to keep all the digits
  l <- gsub("^(.*)e", "'\\1'e", l)
  # turn the 'e+' into plotmath format
  l <- gsub("e", "%*%10^", l)
  # return this as an expression
  parse(text=l)
}


df<- tibble(x=c(0, 10, 20),
            y=c(39600000, 2100000, 122000) )

#plot(x, y, log = "y", type = "b", pch = "21: circle", col = "black", ylab = "CFU/ml", xlab = "Time", frame.plot = FALSE)


ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels=fancy_scientific) +
  labs(title = 'My Title',
     x = 'Time',
     y = 'CFU/ml')


Sincerely,

Nice function.  You could consider removing the + sign on the exponent.  Yousef, I encourage you to figure out what each line does.

 

I believe that you need to make one slight modification:  add trans=’log10’ (sorry about the smart quotes)

 

scale_y_continuous(labels=fancy_scientific,trans='log10')
